The '''Aur system''' was a [[Star system/Legends|star system]] in the [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]] located near<ref name="EGtW:AC" /> the [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> [[Phu/Legends|Phu]].<ref name="EGtW:AC" /> The system contained at least eleven orbital positions, with the ninth and tenth positions being filled by the [[Planet/Legends|planets]] [[Aur IX]] and [[Aur X]], which were in fact [[Diamond/Legends|diamonds]] the size of terrestrial worlds. These huge [[Crystal/Legends|gems]] were believed to have once sat at the cores of [[Gas giant/Legends|gas giants]]. The eleventh orbital position was occupied by a [[Aur system diamond cloud|cloud]] of diamond fragments. These unusual features, termed the [[Aur Diamonds]], led to speculation that the system had been a creation of the ancient [[Celestial/Legends|Celestial]] [[Species/Legends|species]].<ref name="EGtW:AC" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Aur system was originally meant to be mentioned in the [[2012]] source book ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Paul R. Urquhart]], however the sidebar that would have mentioned the system was cut before the book's release. The information regarding the system was then released in [[2013]] as part of ''[[Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut]]'', a series of articles published on the [[StarWars.com]] [[Star Wars Blog|Blog]] by Jason Fry and [[Erich Schoeneweiss]] containing various cut content from ''The Essential Guide to Warfare''.<ref name="EGtW:AC" /> An update to the StarWars.com [[Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion|Online Companion]] to the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', written by [[Daniel Wallace]] and Fry, placed the Aur system in grid square J-13.<ref name="EAOC" />
